newsitem.title: MEXICO: Interest margin forecast to hurt Bancomer.
newsitem.headline: Interest margin forecast to hurt Bancomer.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Bancomer should show limited profits in the second quarter -- below the year-ago period due to Mexico's lower interest rates, analysts said.

A Reuter survey of four analysts estimated the financial group would see earnings per American Depositary Receipt (ADR) of $0.049 for the second quarter, compared with $0.25 in the same period in 1996.
Industry analysts attributed the fall in quarterly earnings to a smaller interest margin because of lower Mexican interest rates compared with 1996.
"Net interest income was very high in 1996 because of higher interest rates," Morgan Stanley analyst Rafael Bello said.
Net profits were seen at about 150 million pesos, compared with 630 million pesos for the same quarter in 1996.
Earnings per ADR in the second quarter will also be below the first quarter's $0.15 per ADR.

"We expect Bancomer earnings to fall due to slightly lower operating revenues conpared with a surprisingly strong 1997 first quarter and an increase in the bank's tax expenses," ING Barings said in a recent report.
Although analysts expect no surprises in the growth of the bank's overdue loan portfolio, they say continuing mortgage problems will influence the group's results.
"Many banks will continue to be affected by the bad mortgage loans and that will not be seen well," said Credit Lyonnais' Andrew Collins.
However ING Barings' analysis said the financial group's earnings would pick up in the second half of the year as long as interest margins improved due to real growth in credit.
Positive influences would come from new support plans for mortgage debtors, but the benefits would not be seen until the next quarter.

"It will be in the second half of this year that we will see these additional programs to halt growth in bad loans being reflectd in the figures," said Araceli Espinosa, banking specialist at BBV-Probursa.
